ITEM-11's CI half is inert as shipped. The diff adds `- 'sdk'` to the `paths:` trigger so a kit-regression gitlink bump fires the visual job, but that job's `actions/checkout@v4` (line 39 of the audited post-image) carries NO `submodules:` key — unlike server-release.yml:37, hub-smoke.yml:52 and desktop-release.yml:38, which all use `submodules: recursive`. Root package.json declares workspaces `['src-app/ui','src-app/desktop/ui','sdk/packages/*']` and package-lock.json records `node_modules/@ziee/kit -> {resolved: 'sdk/packages/kit', link: true}`, so with `sdk/` checked out empty `npm ci` cannot resolve the workspace link and the job dies at 'Install dependencies' before Playwright runs. The design's non-recurrence promise for INV-2 ('a permanent gallery probe ... wire TEST-7 into the gates that actually run') therefore reaches only the LOCAL `npm run gate:ui` path; the one CI job the branch widened the trigger for structurally cannot execute the new spec.

INV-1's guarantee holds only when `bundle_root.is_dir()`. `check_prompt_files` keeps its `if !bundle_present { continue; }` early-out, and the surface the builder's validation PANEL reads always hits it: `handlers/dev.rs:107` (`POST /workflows/validate-def`) calls `validate_collecting(&parsed, &tmp, true)` with a deliberately non-existent tmp root, as does `dev.rs:953`. So on that surface a step naming a `prompt_file:` that is missing / a directory / zero-byte / non-UTF-8 still yields a GREEN panel with Save enabled, and then fails the RUN with 'prompt_file ... cannot be read' — the exact author-visible shape DESIGN §1 quotes from FIX_ROUND-8 ('the panel goes green and Save is enabled ... and fails the RUN'), for cells the design's own table lists as fixed. The acceptance test only ever drives the bundle-PRESENT mode (`validate_collecting(&wf, root.as_path(), false)` with a materialized bundle), so it proves INV-1 for one of the validator's two modes and TEST-4 explicitly concedes the other ('/validate-def has no materialized bundle, so it deliberately reports no file-EXISTENCE verdict'). Mitigating: the run path (runner.rs:1248/1552) does re-validate against the real bundle, so the run fails loudly rather than degenerating.

A row of the same green-then-fail class the design does not list and does not fix: template refs inside a `prompt_file:` BODY. `check_template_refs` (validate.rs) walks only the serialized WorkflowDef, so an inline `prompt: '{{ typo.output }}'` is WORKFLOW_UNKNOWN_STEP_REF (RED), while byte-identical text stored in `prompts/x.md` validates GREEN and then fails the run — `dispatch.rs::resolve_prompt` calls `template::render`, which returns Err on an unresolvable expression (template.rs:316-346) and the dispatcher turns that into StepResult::Failed. That is 'a definition the validator reports GREEN [that] fails at run for a prompt-configuration reason'. It is newly and cheaply closable precisely because of this change: `read_prompt_file` now hands the validator the file BODY, which is the input `check_template_refs` would need. Pre-existing, but squarely inside INV-1 as written and unmentioned by DESIGN §1's table or §3's out-of-scope list.

The acceptance test's advertised assertion is near-tautological; its two hard-coded counts are what actually pin behaviour. Because validate and dispatch now literally call the SAME `prompt_source` + `read_prompt_file`, the `prompt_findings.is_empty() == run.is_ok()` implication is preserved by construction under any change to the shared functions. MUTATION RUN: disabling the emptiness rejection in `read_prompt_file` (`if body.is_empty()` -> `if false && body.is_empty()`) — a direct violation of DESIGN §1's row 8 ('ships the empty prompt to the model that the inline half refuses') — left every one of the 108 implication assertions satisfied and was caught ONLY by `assert_eq!(ran_ok, 18)` (observed 24). The invariant assertion never fired. This is not hollow (the test does go red) but the guard is the aggregate count, not the stated implication: a mutation that swaps which rows are runnable while keeping the count at 18 would pass, and the count is the only thing standing between the matrix and vacuity.

MUTATION RUN, UNCAUGHT. Changing `prompt_file_ref`'s rule from `!s.is_empty()` to `!s.trim().is_empty()` produced ZERO new failures across `cargo test --lib -p ziee -- workflow::` (186 passed, same two pre-existing/introduced failures). The ITEM-10 drift guard `client_prompt_file_predicate_mirrors_prompt_source` is ONE-DIRECTIONAL: it reads stepForms.ts and asserts the TS side rejects '' and does not `.trim()`, but never constrains the Rust side, so a Rust-side change silently desyncs the pair it exists to keep in step.
